claim_tested: Motivation/engagement variables predict later persistence/worsening more strongly than cognitive-control variables
model: Lagged linear model, age 12 to age 15 follow-up
key_result: Motivation/engagement beta = -0.066 (p < .001); cognitive-control beta = -0.031 (p = .003); direct coefficient-comparison p = .043

claim_tested: Motivation/engagement variables predict later persistence/worsening more strongly than executive-control variables
model: Survey-weighted svyglm, age 14 exposure to age 17 follow-up
key_result: Motivation/engagement beta = -0.302 (p < .001); executive-control beta = 0.021 (p = .144); direct coefficient-comparison p < .001

claim_tested: Context moderates motivation/engagement and/or cognitive-control pathways
model: Lagged interaction models with family/sleep/neighborhood moderators
key_result: Context interactions were estimable, but none reached conventional significance (smallest p = .053)

claim_tested: Context moderates motivation/engagement and/or executive-control pathways
model: Survey-weighted svyglm interaction models with family, sleep, and peer moderators to age 17
key_result: 3 of 6 exploratory age-14 context interactions reached nominal conventional significance (smallest p = .003; no multiplicity adjustment)

claim_tested: Genetic scores moderate sensitivity to motivation/engagement or context pathways
model: Survey-weighted svyglm interaction models with depression PRS and cognition PGI plus ancestry PCs to age 17
key_result: Exploratory genetic-score interactions were estimable with ancestry-PC adjustment, but none reached conventional significance
